key_insight: Three-dimensional Cartesian PDE solvers can be reduced exactly to repeated one-dimensional tensor-product line operations, so the “3D matrix” is never assembled, stored, or factored.
engineering_relevance: This lets CFD and PDE solvers achieve linear-time scaling in the number of unknowns while improving memory efficiency and hardware throughput on real parallel machines.
method: Rewrite 3D operators as Kronecker/tensor products of 1D kernels.
Use batched multi-right-hand-side line sweeps and sum factorization for high-order methods.
Apply pencil decomposition for MPI-contiguous directional sweeps and separable direct Poisson/Helmholtz transforms.
evidence_signal: The abstract argues analytically that fixed stencil width or fixed polynomial degree gives O(N) compute and O(Nx+Ny+Nz) storage, with direct separable solvers adding only the expected transform cost.
watch_item: Performance depends on exploiting axis-contiguous data layouts and efficient line-sweep implementations; poor memory layout or communication patterns can erase the theoretical gains.
paper_title: No 3D Matrices: A Unified Tensor-Product View of Matrix-Free Cartesian PDE Solvers
